title: Verbal noun + possessive: A' leughadh mo leabhar
question: What does 'ag ràdh mo sgrùdadh' mean?
correct: Saying my examination/test
explanation: Verbal nouns can be modified by possessives: 'ag ràdh' (saying) + 'mo' (my) + noun.

title: Gerundive construction: A' feuchaint ris
question: What does 'a' feuchaint ris' mean?
correct: Trying (at) it/Attempting it
explanation: 'A' feuchaint ris' means 'trying' or 'attempting', with prepositional object.

title: Causative + object: Leig mi dheth e
question: What does 'leig mi dheth e' mean?
correct: I let him go/I released him
explanation: Causative verbs combine with prepositional pronouns and direct objects.

title: Double object construction: Thug mi leabhar dha
question: What does this mean?
correct: I gave her a book (indirect object)
wrong2: I gave her to book (wrong order)
explanation: 'Thug mi leabhar dha' shows indirect object: 'I gave a book to her'.

title: Impersonal construction: Bhiodh fios agam
question: What does 'bhiodh fios agam' mean?
correct: I would know (conditional impersonal)
explanation: Impersonal verbs with prepositional pronouns: 'bhiodh fios agam' = 'I would know'.

title: Copular: Is breugach e
question: What does 'is breugach e' mean?
correct: He is a liar (identity/characteristic)
explanation: The copula identifies or characterizes: 'Is breugach e' = 'He is a liar'.

title: Existential perfect: Air a bhith ann
question: What does 'tha e air a bhith ann' mean?
correct: He has been there (perfect existential)
explanation: Perfect aspect with existential 'ann': 'has been there'.

title: Subjunctive mood: Ma bhiodh
question: What does 'ma bhiodh e toilichte' mean?
correct: If he were happy (contrary to fact)
explanation: 'Ma bhiodh' (subjunctive) expresses contrary-to-fact conditions.

title: Conditional perfect: Bhiodh mi air dhol
question: What does 'bhiodh mi air dhol' mean?
correct: I would have gone (conditional perfect)
explanation: Conditional perfect combines 'bhiodh' + perfect construction.

title: Negative conditional: Cha bhiodh tu
question: What does 'cha bhiodh tu ag ràdh gur...?' mean?
correct: Wouldn't you say that...? (negative conditional)
explanation: 'Cha bhiodh' is negative conditional; followed by 'gur' (that).

title: Reported speech: Gur e that is
question: What does 'thuirt e gur e Iain a bha ann' mean?
correct: He said that it was Iain (copular reported speech)
explanation: 'Gur e...a th'ann' is the copular reported speech pattern.

title: Direct speech marker: Thuirt i
question: How do you signal direct speech in Gaelic writing?
correct: Use quotation marks and normal word order (VSO)
explanation: Direct speech uses normal Gaelic VSO order within quotation marks.

title: Question in reported speech: An robh?
question: What does 'dh'fhaighnich mi an robh thu ann' mean?
correct: I asked if you were there
wrong2: I asked when you were there
wrong3: I asked why you were there
explanation: 'An robh?' marks yes/no questions in reported speech.

title: Negative question in reported speech: Nach
question: What does 'nach eil' in reported speech mean?
correct: Negative question ('aren't you?') expecting yes
explanation: 'Nach eil' in reported contexts asks 'aren't you?' expecting affirmation.

title: Relative clauses: A bh'ann
question: What does 'an t-àm a bh'ann' mean?
correct: The time that was (past relative)
explanation: 'A bh'ann' is the past relative form: 'an t-àm a bh'ann' = 'the time that was'.

title: Relative future: A bhios
question: What does 'an taigh a bhios math' mean?
correct: The house that will be good (future relative)
explanation: 'A bhios' is the future relative form.

title: Non-finite relative: A dhèanamh
question: What does 'rud a dhèanamh' mean?
correct: A thing to do/A thing for doing (infinitive relative)
explanation: Non-finite relatives use the verbal noun: 'a dhèanamh'.

title: Temporal clause: Nuair a bha
question: What does 'nuair a bha i og' mean?
correct: When she was young (temporal past)
explanation: 'Nuair a' introduces temporal clauses; 'bha' marks past.

title: Temporal: Mu dheireadh
question: What does 'mu dheireadh' mean?
correct: Finally/At last
explanation: 'Mu dheireadh' (around the end) means 'finally' or 'at last'.

title: Temporal: Roimhe
question: What does 'roimhe' mean?
correct: Before/Previously
explanation: 'Roimhe' is an adverb meaning 'before' or 'previously'.

title: Conditional temporal: Gus an
question: What does 'gus an tàinig e' mean?
correct: Until he came (conditional temporal)
explanation: 'Gus an' introduces temporal clauses with a sense of until/up to.

title: Restrictive clause: Nach
question: What does 'nach do thuirt mi' mean?
correct: Didn't I say? (rhetorical restrictive)
explanation: 'Nach' in rhetorical contexts emphasizes negation: 'Didn't I say?'

title: Cleft construction: Is mise
question: What does 'is mise a tha sgìth' mean?
correct: It is I who am tired (cleft — emphatic)
explanation: Cleft constructions use the copula for emphasis: 'is' + pronoun + 'a tha'.

title: Cleft with antecedent: Is e Iain
question: What does 'is e Iain a thubhairt sin' mean?
correct: It was Iain who said that (cleft with proper noun)
wrong3: It is Iain to say that
explanation: Cleft focuses on the subject: 'it was Iain who said'.

title: Pseudocleft: Se am feasgar
question: What does 'se am feasgar a bu chòir dhuinn falbh' mean?
correct: It's in the afternoon that we should leave (pseudocleft)
wrong1: We should leave in the afternoon
wrong2: The afternoon is when we should leave
wrong3: In the afternoon we should leave
explanation: Pseudocleft uses copula + time/manner expression.

title: Tough construction: Tha e doirbh
question: What does 'tha e doirbh a radh' mean?
correct: It is difficult to say (tough construction)
wrong2: It is saying it is difficult
explanation: Tough construction: copula + adjective + infinitive.

title: Resultative: Tha mi sgìth
question: What does 'tha mi sgìth dhen obair' mean?
correct: I am tired from/of the work (resultative state)
explanation: 'Tha mi sgìth' expresses a resultant state.

title: Iterative: A-rithist's a-rithist
question: What does 'a-rithist 's a-rithist' mean?
correct: Again and again/Repeatedly
explanation: 'A-rithist 's a-rithist' means 'repeatedly' or 'again and again'.

title: Habitual past: Bhiodh mi a' snàmh
question: What does 'bhiodh mi a' snàmh an-uairsin' mean?
correct: I used to swim then (habitual past)
explanation: Habitual past uses 'bhiodh' (would) + progressive.

title: Frequentative: Bidh gu tric
question: What does 'bidh mi gu tric ann' mean?
correct: I am often there (frequentative habit)
explanation: 'Gu tric' (often) with 'bidh' expresses frequent habitual action.

title: Durative: Fad greis
question: What does 'bha sin a' dol air adhart fad greis' mean?
correct: That was continuing for a while (durative)
explanation: 'Fad greis' (for a while) marks durative aspect.

title: Continuative: Thig e rithist
question: What does 'chan eil i ann thric a-nis, ach thig i rithist' mean?
correct: She isn't here often now, but will come again (continuative)
wrong1: She is always here and will come
explanation: Continuative shows repeated or resumed action.

title: Inchoative: Thòisich
question: What does 'thòisich i ag ràdh' mean?
correct: She began to say/She started saying (inchoative)
explanation: 'Thòisich' (began) with progressive creates inchoative aspect.

title: Terminative: Chrìochnaich
question: What does 'chrìochnaich e a dhèanamh' mean?
correct: He finished making/doing it (terminative)
explanation: 'Chrìochnaich' (finished) creates terminative aspect.
